Federal Judge Mark Pittman has sought to learn about any deal that may have led to Elon Musk's companies withdrawing their antitrust claims against Apple. Here are the details.

The judge demanded access to any agreement with Apple

Earlier this week, X and SpaceXAI filed a voluntary motion to dismiss, dropping their claims against Apple in a case they brought against Apple and OpenAI last year. The case was concluded with a "no further litigation" order.

According to the original complaint, Apple and OpenAI were accused of colluding through an agreement to integrate ChatGPT into Siri and Apple Intelligence, making it harder for competing AI apps to gain visibility on the App Store. Both Apple and OpenAI have denied the allegations.

In documents filed earlier this week, X and SpaceXAI only stated that they had "resolved the claims against Apple in this case," and emphasised that they were not seeking to withdraw the allegations against OpenAI.

As first reported by POLITICO, Judge Mark Pittman, who has been presiding over the case, ordered X and SpaceXAI to submit to the court "any agreement or combination of agreements reached with Apple to resolve the plaintiffs' claims against Apple in this litigation."

This order was in response to an emergency motion filed by OpenAI, which sought to compel X and SpaceXAI to hand over the agreements they had reached with Apple to settle the dispute. Pittman also ordered the relevant companies to respond to OpenAI's motion by 12 noon that day.
